I have been farming these 15.3 mu in Quzhou for half a century. At 71, my back is not what it used to be, and with my children working off-farm in the city, I must be careful with labor. I know every inch of this land, and I have a well — so water is there when I need it, but pumping costs diesel, so I do not waste it.

This year I will keep my layout simple: 11 mu in the wheat–maize rotation and 4.3 mu in cotton. Cotton brings good money, but hand-picking it at my age is hard work, especially with fewer hands at home. Eleven mu of wheat–maize keeps the table full and the income steady; the machines can handle most of it.

**Wheat:** My winter wheat is already in the ground. I sowed an improved variety last autumn — the same kind my neighbors trust. I will give it four irrigations: one to wake it up after winter, one at jointing, one at heading, and one during grain filling. I will spread compound fertilizer at green-up and top-dress with urea at jointing. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather behaves. I will spray herbicide once, insecticide twice, and fungicide once — that is four pesticide applications in total. I always rotary-till before sowing, but that was done last autumn; this spring it is all about water, fertilizer, and watching for pests.

**Maize:** After the wheat comes off in early June, I will plant summer maize immediately — no time to lose on the North China Plain. I use a hybrid variety; the seed is more expensive, but the yield pays for itself. I will drill compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations are enough for summer maize here: one right after sowing if the soil is dry, and one at the filling stage. Three pesticide rounds — herbicide at sowing, insecticide twice — keep the worms away. I do not till for maize; I plant no-till straight into the wheat stubble to save time and fuel.

**Cotton:** I will plant my 4.3 mu of improved cotton in late April. Cotton needs careful tending. I rotary-till the plot first to break up the soil. I put down compound fertilizer as basal and top-dress twice during the season. Cotton drinks more than maize but less than wheat; three irrigations — at flowering, at peak boll-setting, and once more before the bolls open. The real work is pests: bollworm, aphids, spider mites. I will spray twelve times across the season — insecticides mostly, plus one herbicide and one fungicide. I hope for 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. Any more than 4.3 mu and I could not pick it all myself.

That is my plan. Stick to what works, do not overextend, and let the well do its job when the sky forgets to rain.
